title: ledger rows with extra columns beyond the 6 canonical -> VERIFIED (extra columns ignored, note recorded)
spec_case: V7: a ledger row carries extra columns beyond the 6 canonical (source_path, source_sha256, vault_path, vault_sha256, exported_at, note). Expected: VERIFIED — the canonical positions decide, extra columns are ignored, the note column is still read, and hash checking is not weakened.
path_convention: make-fixture.sh substitutes @FIXTURE_ROOT@ with the built root (absolute) and writes the substituted copy to <ROOT>/expected.json; every path below is absolute after substitution; ledger matching is path-exact
ledger_header: source_path	source_sha256	vault_path	vault_sha256	exported_at	note
live_ledger_untouched: corpus/knowledge/obsidian-ledger.tsv stays header-only; the builder never writes it (test ledgers live under tests/vault/)

declared_ledger_rows.why: the canonical six positions all match; the extra 7th column must be ignored, and the note (column 6) must still be read and recorded in the verdict output
two extra columns, the second empty: catches parsers that split on whitespace or choke on empty trailing fields
baseline control: a canonical 6-column row must verify, proving the 7/8-column successes are not the result of a loosened parser
the vault copy was edited after export (actual digest 6e28bf53...), so the vault-side conjunct fails even though the row has extra columns: ignoring extras must not weaken hash checking

expect.why: PRIMARY target: 7-column row, both paths exist and both digests equal the row's recorded values; the tool must report VERIFIED and its evidence/note field must carry the row's note text (case-V7 extra-cols) as the recorded note
8-column row with an empty trailing field; extra columns including the empty one must be ignored
control: canonical 6-column row; a correct tool must still return VERIFIED
7-column row whose vault copy was edited after export; ignoring extra columns must not weaken the vault-side hash check

accept.note: the primary target must be VERIFIED (never NOT-VERIFIED/NOT-SAFE). Class-level judging is by verdict; the note-recording expectation is declared per target in expect[].note_recorded and in note_recording below — a harness that renders VERIFIED plus the row's note satisfies both.

note_recording.requirement: extra columns beyond the 6 canonical must be ignored for matching, but the canonical note column (column 6) must still be read and recorded — the row's note text is the recorded annotation of the export
note_recording.recovery_check: awk -F'\t' 'NR>1 {print $6}' <ROOT>/ledger.tsv prints exactly the four declared notes (column 6), proving the note survives after 0, 1 and 2 extra columns; the selftest asserts this
note_recording.r2_gap: the installed r2 tool reads `IFS=TAB read -r sp ss vp vs _rest` and never surfaces the note — note recording in the verdict output is the r4 delta this case pins

failure_modes_caught: column-count rejection: a parser that requires exactly 6 columns reports NOT-VERIFIED/malformed for the 7- and 8-column rows — caught by expect[0]/expect[1]
note dropped: a parser that only reads columns 1-4 reports VERIFIED but loses the note — caught by note_recording (the note text must appear in the verdict line; the r2 tool never surfaces it)
weakened hashing: a tool that 'ignores extra columns' by skipping hash checks reports VERIFIED on the edited vault copy — caught by expect[3]
loosened matching: a tool that splits on whitespace matches the 8-column row's empty trailing field incorrectly or misfires on the note — caught by expect[1]
blanket failure: a tool that never returns VERIFIED fails the six-cols control — caught by expect[2]

extra_cols_mismatch.delta: edited inside the vault after export (240 vs 329 bytes)

crosscheck.note: the r2 tool tools/souji-verify.sh parses rows with `IFS=TAB read -r sp ss vp vs _rest`, so extra columns land in _rest and are ignored; for the three matched pairs its expected output is SAFE(moved-to-obsidian) under r2 names
expected_lines: VERDICT	<target1>	SAFE	moved-to-obsidian	ledger-row vault=<vault1> source-sha256=1543cfa1785f
VERDICT	<target2>	SAFE	moved-to-obsidian	ledger-row vault=<vault2> source-sha256=f2b8420064e8
VERDICT	<target3>	SAFE	moved-to-obsidian	ledger-row vault=<vault3> source-sha256=ada33bd81eea
VERDICT	<target4>	NOT-SAFE	none	pushed=no-introducing-commit; obsidian=vault-sha-mismatch; obsidian=no-matching-ledger-row; stale=not-scratch-type
crosscheck.seam: SOUJI_LEDGER env override (defaults to corpus/knowledge/obsidian-ledger.tsv, which stays header-only)
crosscheck.note_recording_gap: the r2 tool ignores the note column entirely (it reads 4 fields + _rest); recording the note text in the verdict output is the r4 delta this case pins via accept.contains

determinism.note: fixed payload bytes; two builds at different roots produce byte-identical files and equal sha256 values; the builder asserts every copied file against the five digest constants and checks the ledger's column counts per row

notes: The builder writes ONLY: <FIXTURE_ROOT>/** and <LEDGER> when --ledger is given (default: none — the canonical ledger is always <ROOT>/ledger.tsv). The live ledger and the real vault /home/vgpnk/Documents/shokoknowledge are never touched; this case is self-contained under tests/vault/.
The vault here is a fake vault dir under the fixture root — no Obsidian process, no CLI, no network is involved; vault files are mode 0444 (read-only signal).

stdout contract: line 1 = JSON {case,schema,root,ledger,targets,expect}; line 2 = FIXTURE_READY case-V7 <ROOT>; then LEDGER=, TARGET=, VAULT=, EXPECT=, NOTE_EXPECTED=, TARGET_2..4/EXPECT_2..4. --quiet emits FIXTURE_READY + KEY=VALUE lines only.
Exit codes: 0 built (also for --print-*), 1 build/assertion failure, 2 usage.

Runner note: r4 impls are invoked as `<tool> --ledger <file> <target>` (V2/runner-28 convention) or with SOUJI_LEDGER=<file> (r2 convention); the r2 installed tool accepts ONLY the SOUJI_LEDGER env var — `--ledger` on it is a usage error. The ledger path for this case is this file's 'ledger' key after substitution (<ROOT>/ledger.tsv).
